thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: unusual sustained TPM increase observed for model-family 'harbor9b' in us-west-2 (3.2x baseline over 5m). Error rate creeping up on routing tier. Paging #oncall.
Maya: on it — looking at dashboard now. pinging @Alex for runtime quota changes if we need to carve capacity.
Alex: I can take quota ops. Maya, any customer-facing 5xx reports? or is this internal throttles?
Maya: Support (Lee) posted a couple of customer 504 reports for chat streams ~5m ago. Not widespread but correlates with the spike. Latency tail increased to ~2.8s p95.
Lee: confirmed, two customers (acct: merchant-42, merchant-77) reported timeouts. CS opened tickets; they asked if we're throttling.
Jordan: Quick ask: can we enable fallback model variant (harbor9b-lite) for non-enterprise traffic and soft-throttle heavy callers? That should reduce token consumption quickly.
Alex: Plan: 1) Apply emergency per-model TPM cap to 4k (was 12k) for harbor9b in us-west-2. 2) Enable routing rule to divert non-critical traffic to harbor9b-lite. 3) Disable function-calling for harbor9b globally to reduce payload bloat. Execute in that order.
Maya: Agree. Do soft-rollout first for routing (no hard cut) and observe 1m. If good, apply TPM cap.
Alex: running command now:

```
# emergency carveout
rictl quota set --model harbor9b --region us-west-2 --tpm 4000 --reason "emergency surge 3254321000"
rictl routing update --name divert-harbor9b-lite --model harbor9b-lite --selector "customer_tier!=enterprise" --percent 30
rictl feature-toggle set --model harbor9b --feature function_calling --enabled false
```

Alex: routing change 30% applied. watching metrics.
Maya: seeing initial drop in token rate for harbor9b within 30s. p50 latency improved.
Jordan: good sign. increase divert to 60%? we need to be careful for enterprise SLAs.
Alex: bumped divert to 60% for non-enterprise.
DeployBot: QUOTA_CHANGE event: harbor9b TPM set to 4000 in us-west-2 by Alex (reason: emergency surge 3254321000). ROUTING_UPDATE event: divert-harbor9b-lite 60% applied.
Lee: CS notified affected customers; sent temporary mitigation note and ETA for update: monitoring.
Maya: function-calling toggle completed by Alex — disabled for harbor9b. expect fewer large payload tokens.
Alex: applied TPM cap now. Monitoring logs show in-flight requests being rate-limited gracefully (429s for excess). We're seeing overall platform token consumption drop ~45% for harbor9b.
Jordan: can you post the exact commands used in the incident ticket? I'll attach them.
Alex: pasted above; also captured audit IDs: quota_audit=qa-3254321, route_audit=ra-3254322, feature_audit=fa-3254323.
Maya: Customer impact summary for the ticket: brief intermittent 504s for two merchants; mitigation applied (routing + TPM cap + disable function-calling) — expected degraded perf for some non-enterprise traffic diverted to harbor9b-lite. No enterprise SLA hit observed so far. Monitoring for 30m, then consider gradual lift.
Lee: CS will keep customers updated every 15m. They've asked for ETA for full recovery — say 30-45m contingent on traffic returning to baseline.
Alex: suggested follow-up: run a short canary to re-enable function-calling for low-traffic partition after 20m, and incrementally raise TPM by 20% if metrics hold.
Maya: handing over to Alex for mitigation ownership and to watch for regressions. I'll stay on the thread for 20m and then transition to post-incident doc.
Alex: oncall ownership accepted. will annotate the incident with audit IDs and times. will escalate to infra if autoscaler engages.
DeployBot: MONITORING: harbor9b error-rate trending down. autoscaler inhibited due to manual cap.
Maya: moving this to postmortem queue: PM-INC-3254321. Leave thread open while Alex watches. :thumbsup:
Alex: noted. I'll update when we start lifting controls.
